answer: Peer graders compare every submission against the ledger corpus and penalise text that overlaps earlier answers, since recycled wording leaves a fingerprint that spreads like a ripple across each clone sharing it. Timing counts as well: a reply filed seconds after the prompt, inside a burst of near-identical accounts, reads as replication rather than reasoning. One detection collapses a whole cluster, so copying stops being cheap. Honest writers keep a steady beacon of distinct phrasing, letting their voice mature like a sonnet whose craft cannot be cloned.
